But several statements are unsupported by the card, and the closing next steps conflict with the rationale. An investigator could use it but would have to redo some work.","problems":["The headline says 99215 rate is elevated in every tier, but the card shows every tier above the all-provider share only in the sense of per-tier comparison; it is fine, yet 'including no chronic conditions' relies on 5 claims in tier 0, which is thin.","Note-quality figures (problems 20%, late 13%, unsigned 0%, data 7%) and 'no audit trail received' are not on the card; they may come from tool output, but 'duplicate and repeated-time rates' are mentioned without any figures given.","The claim that C0084306's documented low MDM bears on C0084436 is a weak link: the cited 99214 is a different claim, and the example claim is billed 99214, not 99215.","C0084309 and C0084448 'for the same patient' is correct (M0035545), but it is only two claims and an abdominal pain dx, which is presented as suspicious with little support.","Next steps are inconsistent with the rationale: the rationale says start with C0084309, C0084448, C0084436, but the next_steps list C0084306, C0084260, C0084275, and C0084306 is a 99214 that is not a 99215 chart; the cited examples are generic low-complexity claims.","Said the documented 99215 charts 'point toward a complex panel' while the excess is not concentrated in sicker patients; this is partly contradictory and only 10 charts support it. The 'comparison providers' 0% figure matches the card's all_provider_rate for 99215 only.","Does not mention that the 10 documented 99215s are not clearly from the low-complexity set: only C0084268 is cited and it is high complexity, so no documented chart covers low-complexity 99215s, a key gap that is only implied."]}
